'''Cimarron River Gas Pipeline''' is a natural gas pipeline in the United States, with 2 segments.

==Location==
Cimarron Expansion Project: The pipeline was proposed to run from Beaver Compressor Station area, Beaver County, Oklahoma to National Helium Gas Processing Plant, Seward County, Kansas.<ref name="r22ec46">{{Cite web|url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2017/12/14/2017-26929.txt|title=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2017/12/14/2017-26929.txt|website=federalregister.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>

==Background==
===Main Line===
The Cimarron River Pipeline is a natural gas pipeline of about 407 miles in Oklahoma and Kansas, operated by Cimarron River Pipeline, LLC.<ref name="r00589c">{{Cite web|url=https://rextag.com/pipeline/cimarron-river-pipeline|title=Cimarron River Pipeline - Rextag Corporation|website=rextag.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref> Rextag lists DCP Midstream, LP as the owner and a system capacity of 0.16 Bcf/d.<ref name="r00589c" /> It receives raw gas from gathering connections in the Anadarko Basin.<ref name="r00589c" />

===Cimarron Expansion Project===
A FERC notice from December 2017 (docket PF17-7-000) said Cimarron River Pipeline LLC planned about 49.3 miles of new pipe in Beaver County, Oklahoma, and Seward County, Kansas. It also planned to lease 19.1 miles of an idle 26-inch pipeline. About 23 miles of the new pipe would be 20-inch and about 24.3 miles would be 30-inch, with short laterals to the National Helium Gas Processing Plant. The project would add up to 631 million standard cubic feet per day of firm capacity.<ref name="r22ec46" />

EIA lists the project as an expansion sponsored by DCP Midstream, cancelled in July 2018 after the anchor shipper withdrew.<ref name="r30800f" />
